must_fix: C011 (confirmed): lines 258-260 falsely attribute a 'disposition' field to dv-coverage-hole-closure; that skill's field is 'hole class'. Fix the sentence to name the correct field, and note that 'disposition' is separately a held noun belonging to dv-tool-bug-testcase-extraction per _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md, so the phrase should not suggest that name was ever a live candidate for this pair of skills.

Add a bounded Grep+Read step (or extend step 1) to retrieve the per-covergroup summary/percentage/weight data that step 2's ranking (sign-off gap and weight, lines 123-125) actually depends on, and add its cost to the retrieval-budget ledger -- or, if weight is meant to be a qualitative/order-of-magnitude judgment rather than a retrieved number, say so explicitly so the agent does not invent a figure.
technical_errors: Lines 258-260: 'bin class and fix kind are local to this skill, named apart from dv-coverage-hole-closure's disposition field on purpose...' -- dv-coverage-hole-closure has no field called 'disposition'; its group-level classification field is 'hole class' (see that skill's line 220: 'hole class : unreachable | not-sampled | model-defect | config-absent | no-stimulus | excluded'). This is the confirmed C011 finding, and it is worse than a simple mislabel: per _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md T3, 'disposition' is a held noun already claimed by an entirely unrelated skill, dv-tool-bug-testcase-extraction ('What the vendor did with the extracted testcase'). So the justifying sentence both invents a field on the cited sibling and, had that name been reused as claimed, would have collided with a different skill's registered meaning. The actual choice made in this skill (bin class / fix kind, correctly local, correctly space-separated per the naming rules) is fine -- only the sentence explaining why is factually wrong and should cite 'hole class', not 'disposition'.
verb_honesty: No violations found. Every point where a tool would need to be run (coverage merge, formal unreachability analysis) is an explicit handoff, never something the agent is told to perform: step 1 (lines 113-116) 'stop and ask the engineer to merge the coverage databases for the test list this disposition is about and to give you the path to the merged text report. The agent cannot merge databases or produce a report, and must never describe what one would have said.'; step 6 (lines 200-205) both unreachability proofs are handoffs -- 'Ask the owner named in the Formal unreachability slot to run the analysis and to give you the path to its text output' and 'Ask the block designer to confirm the encoding cannot occur, and record who said it and when.' All other occurrences of 'merge'/'run' in the body are nouns describing the artifact, not actions assigned to the agent.
hallucination_risks: Low overall. The specific technical claims used (ignore_bins vs illegal_bins error behavior, default-bin exclusion from cross coverage and from the score, option.auto_bin_max, transition-bin (2 => 3) adjacency semantics, option.at_least/weight/per_instance) are generic IEEE 1800 SystemVerilog language semantics, not invented tool flags, message strings, or house conventions, and match the register of domain detail the pack already accepts in dv-ral-bringup's built-in RAL policy table. Nothing proprietary is asserted outside a [[FILL:]] slot.
budget_violations: Step 2 (lines 118-130) ranks unhit bins by (1) sign-off-list membership and how far below its required percentage, and (2) covergroup weight, but the stated budget for step 2 is a single Grep for the Unhit marker (retrieval budget item 2, line 87), and step 1's only Read is 'about 40 lines' at the report header solely to check merge identity (line 108). No step ever Greps or Reads a per-covergroup summary/score/weight table, yet both of step 2's top ranking criteria require exactly that data -- current percentage-vs-goal and weight are not obtainable from a marker-only grep of individual unhit-bin rows (whose declared layout per the Unhit marker slot is just bin name/hit count/goal, line 59). This is a real gap, not a stylistic one: the sibling dv-coverage-hole-closure has a dedicated step for this ('2. Read the totals once, against the goals, and never again' -- one Grep for the summary heading, one 80-line Read, lines 106-114 of that file) performed before any ranking; dv-coverage-hole-disposition has no equivalent step. As written, an agent either invents the percentage/weight figures needed to rank (which the skill itself elsewhere forbids -- 'Do not guess a convention') or silently spends tool calls the budget's own arithmetic (line 94: 'about 37 tool calls at full budget', which otherwise adds up correctly) never accounted for.

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean, check_pack returns zero findings for this slug, role/level are exactly dv-engineer/junior, every declared slot is spent, and every handoff field has an assigning step and agrees with _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md. But the core loop does not close: step 3 is told to "Read the 60-line window at the ranked covergroup's bin table" while step 2 asserts a bin row carries "nothing about the covergroup around it" — so there is no budgeted call mapping the ranked covergroup NAME (from the summary table) to its location in the detail section, and a reader obeying the 39-call ledger ends up dispositioning whatever is concentrated rather than what ranking key 1 (sign-off list, "Nothing else competes") selected. Step 5 separately runs three lookups "in this order" on a budget that funds two Greps and one Read, so out-of-scope is reachable only by skipping the Constraint check. Both are one-sentence fixes, but as it stands the ranking the skill is built around cannot be acted on inside its own budget.
remaining: Step 3 has no budgeted route from a ranked covergroup name to its bin table. Step 2 says a bin row carries 'bin name, hit count, goal, and nothing about the covergroup around it', so the Unhit-marker Grep yields bare line numbers; step 3 then says 'Read the 60-line window at the ranked covergroup's bin table' with no Grep for the covergroup name in the ledger (2/3/3/12/18/0/1 = 39). Following the budget, the reader learns which covergroup a window belongs to only after spending the Read, so ranking key 1 ('On the Sign-off coverage list and below its required percentage ... Nothing else competes') is unreachable and the procedure silently degrades to ranking key 3 (concentration). Fix: budget one Grep per covergroup opened (ledger 39 -> 42) and say so in step 3.

Step 5 spends three lookups on a two-Grep budget. Budget rule 3 grants 'at most two further Grep calls in step 5 -- one in the Test list, one in the Constraint surface OR the Config identity feature list -- and one further 40-line Read'. Step 5 says 'Spend the two Greps of budget rule 3 here, in this order, stopping at the first that settles it' and then runs Stimulus -> Constraint -> Configuration. A hole not settled by the first two must open the Config identity enabled-feature list, which is a third call the budget denies; the Constraint branch has also already consumed the single Read. out-of-scope is a common real class and is only reachable by skipping the Constraint check.

'a failing test contributes no coverage' (When to use something else) is asserted as universal fact and is not one -- coverage is sampled during simulation regardless of the final verdict, and whether a failing run's database is written and merged is a flow policy. The skill handles this correctly everywhere else (the Merge scope slot; step 5's 'A test existing is not a test having run -- cross-check the name against the Merge scope list'), so the flat claim contradicts its own careful handling. The sibling's phrasing ('coverage merged from runs that did not finish is not a closure input') is the honest form.

Nit, gotcha 5: 'Weight decides what a hole costs and is invisible in the bin row. It is a covergroup property' -- option.weight is settable at coverpoint and cross level too, and a cross carrying weight 0 is precisely why a 200-bin hole can cost nothing. Step 4 already lists option.weight among the declaration-level options to read, so the gotcha is narrower than the skill's own procedure.

Nit, step 4: 'A range wider than the field, or written for a previous encoding, can never be hit' -- a wider single range is hit easily (bins b = {[0:31]} on a 4-bit field is hit by 0-15). The unhittable case is a range lying outside the field's representable values, or array bins that split into out-of-range sub-bins. Harmless in practice because the check only runs on already-unhit bins, but loosely stated as a decision rule handed to a junior.

Nit: run id is sourced from Merge scope ('build tag, test list, seed count') while the T3 shape in _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md ties run id to the profile's Run identity fact, which this skill never references. dv-coverage-hole-closure does the same thing, so this is pack practice rather than this skill's defect -- flagged only so it is a deliberate choice.
Nit: semiskill-review-by 2027-04-14 is shared with six other skills including coverage-adjacent dv-config-space-coverage. The pack has larger collisions (9 skills on 2027-09-14), so cosmetic.
new_problems: The step-2 hardening that added 'Neither is in a bin row' and 'nothing about the covergroup around it' is what strands step 3: it forecloses the only zero-cost way to identify a covergroup from a Grep hit without adding the Grep that would replace it. The ledger was updated to 39 for the new step-2 calls but no call was added for step-3 navigation.

The same hardening pass appears to have tightened budget rule 3 to 'two further Grep calls ... one in the Test list, one in the Constraint surface OR the Config identity feature list' while step 5 kept its three-check sequential form ('in this order, stopping at the first that settles it'), leaving the two out of step with each other.
